result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection equipped with high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian signals. However, the environment is vehicle-centric with long crossing distances and sidewalk obstructions from local commercial activity on the left.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Vendor crates and furniture on the left sidewalk narrow the accessible path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the crossing to provide a safe waiting area mid-crossing.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, paved sidewalk with active commercial frontage and residential units above. However, the walkway is cluttered with structural awning supports and lacks a physical buffer from the adjacent roadway and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Structural Obstructions
hazards.description: Metal poles supporting the overhead awning are located in the middle of the sidewalk, creating a tripping hazard and narrowing the effective walking path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left foreground on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation (like trees or bollards) between the sidewalk and the travel lane, exposing pedestrians to traffic.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large parked vehicle on the right side of the frame blocks the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install street trees or large planters along the curb to create a vertical buffer between pedestrians and moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the nearest intersection to improve visibility and reduce crossing distances.

interventions.title: Bollards or Flexible Posts
interventions.description: Install bollards near the curb to provide physical protection from vehicle incursions.

result.summary: The street environment is a narrow commercial corridor where the pedestrian walkway is significantly obstructed by market stalls and a large temporary structure, forcing pedestrians into the roadway. While the narrow street width likely naturally calms traffic, the lack of clear, dedicated pedestrian space and the presence of parked vehicles create potential conflicts.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction (Shed)
hazards.description: A large blue shed completely blocks the sidewalk on the right side of the image, forcing pedestrians into the street.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction (Market Stalls)
hazards.description: Goods and stalls extend into the walkway on the right, further reducing pedestrian space.

hazards.name: Narrow Shared Space
hazards.description: Pedestrians are forced into the travel lane due to sidewalk blockages, with no physical separation from vehicles.

interventions.title: Shared Street (Woonerf) Conversion
interventions.description: Redesign the street as a level-surface shared space with clear pedestrian priority and traffic calming elements to formalize the existing usage.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance Enforcement
interventions.description: Ensure a minimum clear through-zone is maintained on sidewalks by regulating the size and placement of outdoor structures and market stalls.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, covered sidewalk fronting active commercial businesses, providing excellent protection from the elements. However, the walkway is cluttered with trash bins and display tables, and structural awning supports create obstacles within the pedestrian path. There is no visible buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, and crossing infrastructure is not present in this mid-block view.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Large trash bins and display tables significantly narrow the effective walking width and may force pedestrians to walk closer to the curb.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground on the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Structural Supports
hazards.description: Vertical poles supporting the awning are located in the middle of the sidewalk, creating potential tripping hazards and sightline obstructions.

interventions.title: Designated Furniture and Display Zones
interventions.description: Establish clear zones for commercial displays and waste management to ensure a continuous, unobstructed pedestrian clear path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Buffer
interventions.description: Install bollards, planters, or street furniture at the curb to provide a physical and psychological barrier between pedestrians and moving traffic.
